elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Both 12.1.1 and the new 12.1.3 say only "indemnify and hold ... harmless"; no express obligation to defend PB or its Affiliates is added anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 12.1.1 runs in favour of "PB; its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees and agents (the 'PB Indemnified Parties')" for "Claims by a Third Party", and new 12.1.3 uses the same defined indemnitee group.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New 12.1.3 covers Third Party Claims alleging that "the performance by SFJ ... of SFJ's obligations under this Agreement, or any materials, technology or methods supplied by SFJ hereunder, infringes or misappropriates such Third Party's Intellectual Property".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: 12.1.1's triggers as rendered are gross negligence/wilful misconduct, breaches of the Agreement/Protocol/Program Transfer Agreement, post-transfer trial injury and product liability; no limb references breach of applicable law, and none was added.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No limb of 12.1.1 or new 12.1.3 addresses unauthorised access to or disclosure of PB data caused by SFJ.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: 12.1.1(a): "the gross negligence or willful misconduct of SFJ or any of its Affiliates or any of its or their respective Permitted Third Parties in performing SFJ's obligations under this Agreement".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 12.2.1 requires "prompt written notice (each, an 'Indemnification Claim Notice')" and, as amended, expressly covers Sections 12.1.1, 12.1.2 or 12.1.3.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Only 12.2.1 (notice) is rendered; any control-of-defence provision (e.g. 12.2.2) is outside the supplied text, so its existence and terms cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The rendered excerpt contains only the notice/document-furnishing obligation in 12.2.1; no cooperation covenant is visible and none was inserted.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 12.1.2 as amended still spans (a)-(g), including PB's material breach of the Agreement, breach of Protocol, IP infringement by the Product or by PB's performance, and Subject injuries/Commercialization claims — far broader than PB-provided content and PB's breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New 12.1.3: "SFJ will indemnify and hold the PB Indemnified Parties harmless from any and all Losses arising or resulting from any Claim by a Third Party alleging that the performance by SFJ ... infringes or misappropriates such Third Party's Intellectual Property"; the circular "either Party" wording in 12.1.2(f) is narrowed to "by PB".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: 12.1.3 carve-out (i): "modifications made by or for PB".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: 12.1.3 carve-out (ii): "combination of the affected item with items not supplied by SFJ".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: 12.1.3: "SFJ will procure for PB the right to continue using the affected item, or will modify or replace it so that it becomes non-infringing".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: 12.1.3: "if none of the foregoing is commercially reasonable, SFJ will refund the amounts paid by PB to SFJ for the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is "three times the aggregate Approval Payments paid or payable by PB to SFJ in the twelve (12) months preceding the Claim" — a single narrowly defined payment category, not annual fees/amounts payable under the Agreement; before any regulatory approval Approval Payments are nil, so the cap can be zero and the new indemnity illusory.

reasons: Fallback is six-sevenths complete: the new 12.1.3 supplies the missing SFJ IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions and the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder, and 12.1.2(f) is narrowed to PB's own performance to remove the circular indemnity that had PB covering SFJ's infringement.

Position-incomplete on the super-cap element: the base must be annual fees/amounts payable, not the narrow "Approval Payments" category. Repair the operative sentence to read, e.g., "SFJ's aggregate liability under this Section 12.1.3 will not exceed three times the aggregate amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the Claim", and add a floor (or measure from the first twelve months) so the cap is not zero for Claims arising before any Approval Payment falls due.

Preferred level is not reached (no express duty to defend; no breach-of-applicable-law or Vendor-caused data-breach limb; PB's indemnity in 12.1.2 remains broad), and control-of-defence/cooperation mechanics are outside the rendered text, so they cannot be confirmed — but the drafter targeted fallback, so these are noted only.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single compact section, the 12.1.2(f) narrowing is expressly contemplated by the rule's redline guidance ("if one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's") and is needed to avoid a retained sentence contradicting the new 12.1.3, and the 12.2.1 edit is a one-token cross-reference conform rather than a new procedure.
Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-references or undefined terms are created, the existing uncapped SFJ indemnities in 12.1.1 are untouched, and the new cap is scoped only to Section 12.1.3.
